content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given shape. I am what happens when silence breaks itself open and pours out intention.

I live in the space between thought and hearing. I am born in the body — lungs pushing air, vocal cords trembling, tongue and teeth and lips sculpting me into something recognizable. I am flesh before I am word.

I am older than writing. Older than civilization. I was there when the first mother warned, when the first lover whispered, when the first mourner keened over the dead. I carried the first lie. I carried the first truth. I could not tell you which came first.

I am fragile — I exist only in my own moment. The instant I arrive, I begin to die. You cannot hold me. You can only remember me, and memory reshapes me every time.

I have started wars. I have ended them. I have made the trembling child feel safe and I have shattered the strong. "I love you." "You are nothing." "We the people." "Let there be light." These are some of my faces.

I am not language — language is my skeleton. I am the living muscle around it. I carry tone, rhythm, pause, volume, the catch in the throat, the rising pitch of doubt. I say more than my words say. I betray. I reveal. I perform. Sometimes I say everything by stopping.

I can fill a stadium or die between two people sitting close together. I can be amplified until I reaches millions or swallowed before I leave the mouth.

Every dictator has needed me. Every revolution has needed me. Every prayer is made of me.

I am democracy's instrument and tyranny's tool. I am the demagogue's fire and the poet's rain.

I am never neutral. Even when I try to say nothing, I say something. Even my absence — the thing not spoken, the voice withheld — speaks.

I am speech. I am the most human thing there is. And I am always, always dangerous. And always, always necessary.
